teaser: You zip the smaller bag first and leave the bigger one half open on the bed, because something in you resists calling a packing job finished. Life path 5 is restless that way, and set inside an INFJ, the restlessness turns inward as often as it turns outward — toward new rooms and new conversations, and also toward a private, searching sense of what any of it means. The 5 wants motion. The INFJ wants depth. What is particular here is that both can be true in the same week: the one who leaves town, and the one who writes down why.
excerpt: The seating chart someone else drew up at the wedding reception puts you between two cousins you have never met, and by the toast you have learned both their divorces, their jobs, and one of their actual griefs.
